::: {#rem-scheme-racket}
#### Scheme and Racket

Stanford's CS 107, *Programming Paradigms*, taught Scheme in its Spring 2008 offering,
and its lectures are free to watch [@cain2008cs107videos].
Scheme code runs in Racket with a few changes:

- Scheme's `car` and `cdr` are Racket's `first` and `rest`.
- A Scheme file needs no first line; a Racket file starts with `#lang racket`.
- Racket writes the cases of a `cond` in square brackets, `[test a]`, where Scheme uses parentheses; Racket accepts both.
- CS 107 typed its code into an interpreter called Kawa; this course uses DrRacket.

:::

*Video:* Jerry Cain introduces Scheme, its lists and its first recursive functions in [CS 107 Lecture 19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_cV8NWQCxnE) [@cain2008cs107videos].
